chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Ahmad ibn Ismail the scribe, from his father, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was in the Sacred Mosque, and a group from the Quraysh looked at him and said, 'Who is this?' It was said to them, 'The Imam of the people of Iraq.' Some of them said, 'Send one of you to him to ask him.' So a young man from them came to him and said to him, 'O cousin, what is the greatest of the major sins?' He said: 'Drinking wine.'

He went to them and informed them, so they said to him, 'Go back to him.' So he went back to him, and he said to him, 'Did I not tell you, O cousin, drinking wine?' He went to them and informed them, so they said to him, 'Go back to him.' They did not cease with him until he went back to him and asked him. He said to him, 'Did I not tell you, O cousin, drinking wine?'

Indeed, drinking wine causes its drinker to enter into adultery, and theft, and the murder of the soul which Allah has prohibited, and into associating partners with Allah. And the effects of wine override every sin, just as its tree climbs over every tree.
ai.seo_question: What is the greatest major sin according to Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) identifies drinking wine as the greatest major sin (*akbar al-kaba'ir*) during a dialogue with Quraysh in the Sacred Mosque. He elaborates that wine is the 'root' of all sins, leading to adultery, theft, and murder, using the metaphor of its tree overshadowing others to illustrate its pervasive corrupting influence. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on wine not merely as a standalone prohibition, but as the catalyst for a cascade of moral and spiritual decay.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Amro Bin Usman, form Ahmad Bin Ismail the scribe, from his father who said,

‘I met Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> in the Sacred Masjid, so a group from the Quryesh looked at him<sup>asws</sup>, so they said, ‘Who is this?’ So it was said to them, ‘An Imam<sup>asws</sup> of the people of Al-Iraq’. So one of them said, ‘If we could send one of you to him<sup>asws</sup>, ask him<sup>asws</sup>’. So a youth from them came over to him<sup>asws</sup>, so he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘O cousin, what is the biggest of the major sins?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Drinking the wine’.

So he went over to them, so they said to him, ‘Reiterate to him<sup>asws</sup>’. So he reiterated to him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Did I<sup>asws</sup> not tell you, O cousin, drinking the wine?’ So he went to them and informed them, so they said, ‘Reiterate to him<sup>asws</sup>’. So they did not cease with it until he reiterated to him<sup>asws</sup>, so he asked him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Did I<sup>asws</sup> not tell you, O cousin, drinking the wine?

Drinking the wine enters its perpetrator into the adultery, and the theft, and the murder of the soul which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Prohibited, and into the association with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> (Shirk), and the effects of the wine override upon every sin just as its tree overrides (climbs) upon every tree’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Amr ibn ‘Uthman from Ahmad ibn ’Isma‘il al-Katib from his father who has said the following: “Once abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, went to Masjid al-Haram (the Sacred area). A group of Quraysh saw him. They asked, ‘Who is he?’ It was said to them, ‘He is the Imam of the people of Iraq.’ Certain ones among them said, ‘You may send someone to ask him questions.’ One young man from among them went and asked, ‘Son of my uncle, what is the greatest of the great sins?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is drinking wine.’
He went back and informed them about it. They said, ‘Go back and ask again.’ He went back and he (the Imam) said, ‘Did I not say, O son of a brother, that it is drinking wine?’

He went back and informed them and they told him to go back again. They were there that he went back to him (the Imam) and asked him. He (the Imam) said, ‘Did I not say, O son of a brother that it is drinking wine?
Drinking wine takes the drinker to fornication, theft, murder of what Allah has prohibited, paganism and the effects of wine goes above all sins like trees that go above all other trees.’”
